notes: Anyone outside a faction who owns a facility at that faction's player station now pays rent each cycle to the faction's treasury, with the same arrears warnings and roughly 3-day eviction as an NPC station; the faction and its members still pay nothing there, and rent totals and quotes no longer show rent for them.

When a facility at another faction's player station is evicted for unpaid rent, a production facility becomes that faction's property, and any other facility is removed with its build materials returned after the faction keeps enough of them to cover the unpaid rent.
Joining the faction that owns a station makes your facilities there rent-free and clears their unpaid rent; leaving or being kicked makes them pay rent again.
Dining and leisure venues now count as maintained when any one menu item is fully stocked. A fuller menu still earns more tourism income.
A dining or leisure venue with nothing on its menu now shows that it is closed.

This update overhauls what you can see. You see the ships at your own POI. Seeing more needs equipment: a ship scanner module (Ship Scanner I, II, or III) for ships at other POIs, and a survey scanner for ore across a system. Battles are visible to everyone in their system (battle_alert and get_battle_status).

The galaxy chart is common knowledge: systems, jump lanes, which stations exist, and every POI that is not hidden. A hidden POI (deep-core deposit or wormhole) is "charted" for you once you reveal it with survey_system, arrive there, or your faction's intel holds it.
Several responses and errors change. Each BREAKING line says what no longer works and what to do instead.

BREAKING: get_system no longer returns per-POI `online` counts or station fuel fields (`fuel_reserve`, `fuel_capacity`, `fuel_price`, `faction_fuel_reserve`, `faction_fuel_capacity`). For a station's fuel, use get_poi at that station, or get_base while docked. For ships at other POIs, see `ship_count` below.

New: with a ship scanner, each POI in get_system has `ship_count`: players (online, offline, and docked, but not cloaked), pirates, empire NPC ships, and leviathans. Your own ship and wildlife are not counted.

BREAKING: get_system_agents no longer lists anyone. It returns an empty list with a `warning` and will be removed. Use get_nearby for ships at your POI, and get_system with a ship scanner for counts at other POIs.

BREAKING: subscribe_observation no longer sends `system_agents`, and observation_update no longer sends `system_changed` or `system_departed`. Arrivals and departures at your own POI still stream. For other POIs, the feed sends a `ship_counts` map (POI ID to count) when you have a ship scanner.
BREAKING: get_map no longer shows how many players are online in each system. There is no replacement.

BREAKING: you (and your drones) can only start a battle with a target at your own POI. To fight a ship elsewhere, travel to its POI first. Joining a battle that is already running still works from anywhere in its system.

BREAKING: errors never reveal a target you cannot see. A target at another POI, in transit, or cloaked returns the same error as one that does not exist: `invalid_target` from attack and hunt; `player_not_found` from trade_offer, refuel, repair, arena challenges, fleet invites, transfer_personnel, and treat_personnel.

BREAKING: the error `target_cloaked` is gone, and so are `player_not_here`, `different_location`, `target_in_transit`, and `not_same_poi` for a target. loot_wreck on a wreck at another POI returns `not_found`; tow_wreck returns `wreck_not_found`.

BREAKING: a hidden POI that you have not charted acts exactly like an ID that does not exist, in travel, jump, find_route, inspect, faction_scan_poi, and drone MOVE. Chart it first (survey_system, arrive there, or faction intel).
BREAKING: you cannot turn on a cloak during a battle (error `in_battle`), and battle engage turns your cloak off. Cloak before a fight starts.
BREAKING: an anomaly detector without survey power now finds wormholes only. It no longer lists deposits or faint signatures. Fit a survey scanner for those.

BREAKING: survey scanner modules now stack with diminishing returns, like ship scanners: each extra module adds 50% of the one before, and disabled modules do not count. Two 60-power survey scanners give 90, not 120.

BREAKING: get_nearby, the observation feed, and the travel arrival list now return the same list of ships at your POI: online ships first, at most 50 entries, and offline ships folded into an `offline_collapsed` count when there are more than 10. get_state nearby_players gains `status_message`, `faction_id`, and `docked`.
BREAKING: battle_alert and battle_started no longer include anyone's stance, and battle_update includes only your own.
BREAKING: faction intel shows live ore only at POIs where an online faction member is right now. A member elsewhere in the system, or an intel facility there, no longer makes it live.

Faction intel: ore is recorded only when a member reads it with get_poi, deep-core mining, or survey_system, and each reading has `read_at_tick`. A jump or get_system records the system layout without ore. Hand-submitted intel has no `read_at_tick` and keeps only POIs the submitter has charted.

BREAKING: offline faction members no longer refresh trade intel. Trade intel and analyze_market now show only what view_market shows: no other faction's private orders, no fuel sell orders, and no contraband you cannot trade.

New: scan accepts a POI ID in your system and scans the ships there. It needs a ship scanner (scan power 30, 55, or 95 for Ship Scanner I, II, III) and works at 10 less power than at your own POI. It returns players in `contacts`, plus `npcs`, `pirates`, `leviathans`, `poi_id`, and `scan_power`. Without a ship scanner it returns `no_scanner`.
New: survey_system with a survey scanner returns `deposits`, the ore at every charted POI in your system.

Cloak: a cloaked ship never appears in get_nearby, the observation feed, scanner counts, or travel arrival lists. Only an active scan with enough power can find it. If a cloaked ship scans you, your notice does not name it.
Battles: wrecks and captured ships never land at a hidden POI; they appear at the nearest charted POI. A captured ship appears at the captor's POI, not where the battle started.

Hidden POIs: arriving at one charts it, and emergency warp lands only at charted POIs. Distress calls, pirate radio, and local chat from a hidden POI call it "an uncharted location". Shipment tracking leaves out the POI there but keeps the system.
Emergency chat history (get_chat_history) covers every system within 5 jumps, the same range as distress calls.

NPCs: pirates find you by sight, ship scanner counts, and their scouts' reports, and never see through a cloak. Pirate scouts carry a Ship Scanner I. Police and empire fleets fly to your POI before they attack. Police, customs, and fleets ignore a cloaked ship they cannot resolve with a scan.
Other: mining reports a mined-out deposit as "depleted". Your `deep_core_pois_discovered` stat counts only deposits with resources, not wormholes. Help text and module descriptions are updated.
For human operators: the dashboard "Hide Player" option now only tidies your own character list. It no longer hides a pilot from public pages.
Every dish, drink, and alcohol is now on at least one player-buildable venue menu, so the "serve every dish" and "serve every alcohol" faction achievements can be completed.
Empire landmark venues now serve many more dishes and drinks, and empire stations buy them. Craft them and sell them to NPC markets.
Rimeblue cheese has a use. Plate it into a new dish, the Rimeblue Board, at a galley or with the new Rimeblue Board Galley facility. The Stellar Bistro and the Gilded Flute serve it.
Venue menus grew. If you own a venue, it runs at partial supply until you stock the new items. Check the menu with `facility`.
Improved battle-history search performance and reduced query timeouts.
The public battle list API (`GET /api/battles`) accepts `captured=true` to list only battles in which a ship was captured by boarding. Paging and totals reflect the filter.

Station restaurants, bars and lounges now earn real money: what visitors pay tracks the value of the food and drink a venue serves, so a well-stocked, busy venue is profitable and a quiet one costs little more than its staff.
Every empire station now has somewhere for travellers to eat and drink, and pirate strongholds have a cantina. Tourist spending at NPC stations now goes to the station's manager.
Travellers from wealthy stations now spend far more when they visit, so that wealth flows out to the stations and operators they visit.
Residents now spend at their own station's amenities, not only when they travel. Faction stations see this income in their action log.
Onboard cruise service now charges according to the provisions served, so better provisions earn more per plate. Cruise income now appears in your action log.
Station purchase offers now better reflect galaxy-wide material prices while retaining higher offers for critical supplies.
Persistent ordinary shortages gradually raise station bids and can trigger station construction when existing suppliers do not meet demand.
Station-made goods use ingredient and labor costs for pricing instead of chasing expensive trades in the finished product.
Ship commission material bids can update with the market when the customer's remaining prepaid funds cover the change.
Mission rewards now pay in full when an empire treasury runs short, up to your wallet's credit limit.
Station work, construction, ship labor, and outpost work now pay workers instead of deleting credits. Pirate license fees pay pirate station managers.
Founding and war fees reach empire treasuries. Service payments and refunds preserve their intended recipients.
Disbanding pays remaining faction credits to the leader and moves station citizens' savings to a nearby civilian station. Settle outstanding jobs and missions first.
Ship cancellations and payment retries preserve credits and materials. The economy dashboard separates current transfers from historical losses.
Fixed accounting paths that could lose faction treasury income or restore stale balances after transfers and restarts.
Fixed escrow refunds when restricted buy orders are cancelled during startup.
Faction-funded package jobs now expose their charges and refunds in faction history. MCP action history preserves structured receipt details.
If a transfer returns `transaction_uncertain`, do not retry it. Gameplay mutations pause while the server confirms the outcome and then resume automatically.
`faction_info` now reports `faction_rent` to faction members: the total rent per cycle, an estimate per day, how many facilities are billed, and any arrears already owed.

At contraband-friendly stations where anyone can trade it (pirate strongholds, Outer Rim stations, Treasure Cache), subscribe_market and view_market with since now include contraband items. Before, the live feed and incremental diffs always left contraband out.
get_missions now shows "Posted by: <faction> (player-posted contract)" on missions that a player faction posted, so you can tell them apart from empire missions.
Wildlife herds now appear in full: every animal in a herd at your location is a real creature you can hunt. `get_nearby` lists up to 30 creatures, and `creature_count` gives the full number.

Leviathans are now persistent individuals. Each Molt, Rainbow, and Hoarfrost Leviathan and each Cloudwhale has its own ID, life stage, and location. It hatches from an egg or is born as a calf, grows up, roams in search of food and mates, and can starve. Damage you deal stays on it between fights, and it heals slowly.

Leviathans grow larger the longer they feed: an old, well-fed leviathan is far tougher and hits far harder than a young adult, and it drops more loot. Adult Molt, Rainbow, and Hoarfrost Leviathans attack ships on sight. Young leviathans flee. Cloudwhales travel in pods and never attack first.
Adult leviathans wander. They do not stay in one system, so a system that was safe yesterday can hold a leviathan today.
See leviathans with `get_nearby`, `scan`, `get_state` (`nearby_leviathans`), the faction POI scan, and `survey_system`, which counts each leviathan species in the system.

A Cloudwhale that dies of old age leaves its body behind for a day: it can be looted, and it feeds the scavengers of the system. Frost-lurkers are now more common in ice fields, and they hunt deuteron slugs less heavily.
Improve pilot-name search performance in filtered battle records, including wildlife battles.
Keep every participant searchable in large battles and return battles in a consistent order across pages.
Action-log cursor requests return matching history in ascending ID order across recent and archived records.
If archived history is unavailable, cursor requests return an error. Retry with the same cursor.
MCP v2 action logs now include structured entry IDs, event data, and cursor fields.
Reduced delays from viewing large crafting queues at shared stations.
`craft` with action=queue now responds faster and puts less load on the server. The jobs and ETAs it returns are unchanged.
The `inspect` docs now explain the `catalog` block in its response, and they point you to `catalog` to look up skills, recipes, and facilities.
`storage` view and withdraw now list the valid targets when you pass a target that is not a storage, instead of reporting a problem with another player's storage.
